Published online:
    September 10, 2026

Geographic focus:
    United States (with secondary reference to Europe/Middle East)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [NO]
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES]

Synopsis:
    Hot PPI data (+5.4% YoY through August) and stable jobless claims have nudged Fed rate hike odds higher ahead of the Sep 15-16 FOMC meeting. Inflation drivers include Middle East conflict disrupting oil supply and AI-driven electronics demand. Hike probability moved from ~65% to ~70% for next week, with markets near-certain of one to two hikes by year-end. The decisive near-term trigger is Friday's core CPI print. The ECB has already moved, hiking rates amid Iran-war-driven oil above $100/bbl. Fed policy rate currently sits at 3.50%-3.75%, and inflation has remained above the 2% target for 5.5 years.

Q01. Is the content's main message on the US economy, US yields, US interest rates?
Relevance: YES (the article centers on Fed rate hike expectations, US inflation data, and monetary policy trajectory)

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 90 (strongly focused on the probability and timing of a Fed rate hike)
Probability of increase: 70% (near-term, Sep 15-16 meeting); near-certain for at least one hike by year-end per market pricing

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 20 (holding is presented only as a residual scenario contingent on Friday's CPI)
Probability of holding: 30% (implied inverse of the 70% hike probability for the Sep meeting)

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 0 (no mention of cuts whatsoever)
Probability of decrease: 0%

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: 70 (Meaningfully more hawkish — PPI came in hot, hike odds moved up from 65% to 70%, Capital Economics flagging hikes likely even if not September, ECB already moving; only restraint is awaiting Friday's core CPI)
